algorithm: Sequence numbers select the newest version. WAL persists before memtable mutation. Flush publishes the durable SST then updates the manifest before resetting the WAL. Compaction writes a replacement and publishes the manifest before deleting old tables. Reference: https://www.cs.umb.edu/~poneil/lsmtree.pdf .
architecture: Mutation → durable WAL → MemTable. Flush → immutable SST → durable manifest checkpoint. Get merges memtable/table versions. Recovery replays WAL records newer than the checkpoint.
data_model: WAL record = sequence, key, value, deleted. SST payload includes sorted key versions and a Bloom bitmap. Manifest lists authoritative tables, checkpoint and generation.
description: A durable local single-writer engine with checksummed WAL frames, immutable tables, Bloom filters and manifest-based compaction.
design: Keep tombstones during compaction to make deletion semantics explicit. Orphan files are ignored; only manifest-listed tables are authoritative. A torn tail differs from corruption of a complete frame.
family_notes: Overwrite repeated keys and preserve the latest sequence.
Apply tombstones and compare against an independent dictionary.
Flush a small memtable into immutable sorted tables.
Merge multiple tables without resurrecting deleted records.
Restart using the WAL and append another durable record.
Discard only an incomplete trailing WAL frame and preserve subsequent recovery.
limitations: Python single-writer reference, not a distributed C++/Rust database. SST files are JSON and read in full, so lookup performance is intentionally limited. No cross-process locking, replication, snapshots, concurrent reads during writes, memory mapping or background compaction. Incomplete final WAL frames are truncated; complete checksum corruption fails closed.
operations: Use a private directory and one writer. Back up manifest and listed tables together. Test filesystem-specific durability before promising crash guarantees on remote or unusual filesystems.
scope: POSIX-style fsync, checksummed framed WAL, in-memory latest records, sorted checksummed SST files, Bloom lookups, atomic manifest updates, full-table compaction and restart recovery.
security: Treat this as educational code; review it before handling trusted data.
title: Log-Structured Merge-Tree Storage Engine
